title: Prototype Pollution in Recursive Object Merging
platform_conditions: ECMAScript 2020 semantics in Node.js runtime; identical in browsers wherever recursive merge or path assignment runs
security_mechanism: Ordinary objects inherit from Object.prototype, and plain assignment to __proto__ or to a path ending in constructor.prototype does not create an own property -- it re-points the prototype chain or walks to Function.prototype. A recursive merge (or a dot/bracket path setter) that copies attacker keys without filtering therefore lets JSON like {"__proto__":{"isAdmin":true}} change what every later object in the process inherits. Property lookups on unrelated objects then find attacker-chosen values, which frequently flips security-relevant option flags (isAdmin, privileged, safeMode) that guards read indirectly.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies, JSON payloads, query strings, or any nested object parsed from attacker-controlled input that reaches a deep-merge, defaults-fill, or path-based set operation.
source_sink_clues.sink: Recursive merge helpers writing target[key] = value for attacker keys (especially __proto__ and constructor); lodash-style set/assign with path strings; obj[attackerPath] = value on plain objects

tracking_guards: Check the merge skips or hard-freezes the dangerous keys (__proto__, constructor, prototype) before assignment, uses Object.create(null) targets or a Map instead of plain objects, or parses with a JSON reviver that drops inherited keys; assignment through defineProperty alone is not a guard unless the key check is also present.
not_candidate_when: The merged keys come from a fixed server-side schema and unknown keys are rejected before the merge, the target is an Object.create(null) dictionary immune to prototype writes, or the input is a top-level copy (Object.assign / spread) whose keys can never be nested paths.
public_references: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html
OWASP Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Prototype_Pollution_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
